name: Caraway
summary: An anise-adjacent seed with a warm, slightly bitter, licorice-tinged flavour. Essential in North African chile pastes and Central European baking.
description: Caraway seeds resemble cumin but taste quite different — they carry a warm anise character without being as intensely liquorice as fennel. They are the defining flavour of harissa and many North African spice pastes, as well as rye breads, sauerkraut, and Central European dishes. Toast lightly before using to bring out their volatile oils. Caraway bridges savoury spice cooking and baking like few other seeds.
